goal: Sign on to the MeridianCore servicing console, open Member Servicing, look up the member whose number is given by the member_id input, and read that member's Regular Savings account: its current balance and its status. Also read the member's name from the member record.
summary:
Signed on to MeridianCore, navigated to Member Servicing, acknowledged the one-time system notice, searched for member 100244, and retrieved the Regular Savings account details: Current Balance $4,812.37, Status OPEN, and Member Name ([REDACTED]:output:member_name) from the member record. // Probed all four failure/edge scenarios on the live session:
1. Non-existent member (999999): Console shows 'No member matching that number was found.' with the searched number - registered as return_to_caller outcome 'member_not_found'.
2. Restricted executive-services member (100999): Console shows 'Access Restricted' / 'You do not have permission to view this member.' with a 'Supervisor Override' button available on the same session - registered as escalate_to_human outcome 'executive_services_restricted'.
3. One-time System Notice interstitial (scheduled maintenance window) appeared before the first Member Servicing search after sign-on, cleared via 'Acknowledge and Continue' button - registered as recovery 'system_maintenance_notice'.
4. Deliberate sandbox host fault when re-looking up member 100244: 'Application Error' / 'SYSTEM ERROR MC-5001' - 'The host transaction could not be completed. Contact the service desk with this reference.' - registered as declare_failure 'host_transaction_error' since this must stop the run rather than be treated as a valid answer.

actions.expect: Member Servicing menu or main console page appears

actions.intent: Open Member Servicing to look up the member
Acknowledge the system notice to proceed to Member Servicing
Enter the member number to look up
Search for the member's account summary
actions.expect: Member record with account summary appears

actions.intent: Return to Member Servicing lookup to test non-existent member number
Enter a non-existent member number to test error handling
Search for the non-existent member to observe error message
actions.expect: An error or not-found message appears

actions.intent: Start a new search to test the executive-services restricted member
Enter the executive-services restricted member number to test entitlement handling
Search for the restricted executive-services member to observe entitlement error
actions.expect: An entitlement or restriction message appears

actions.intent: Return to Member Servicing lookup to test the deliberate host fault on member 100244
Enter member 100244 again to trigger the deliberate host fault state
Search for member 100244 to trigger the deliberate sandbox host fault

declared_outcomes.name: member_not_found
declared_outcomes.marker_text: No member matching that number was found.
declared_outcomes.message: The searched member number does not exist in the system. The console displays 'No member matching that number was found.' along with the searched member number.

declared_outcomes.name: executive_services_restricted
declared_outcomes.marker_text: You do not have permission to view this member.
declared_outcomes.message: Member 100999 is flagged EXECUTIVE SERVICES. A supervisor override is required to continue. A supervisor can clear this block on the same session via the 'Supervisor Override' button.
declared_outcomes.remediation: Have a supervisor click 'Supervisor Override' on this same session to clear the restriction and continue the lookup.

declared_recoveries.name: system_maintenance_notice
declared_recoveries.marker_text: Scheduled maintenance window 02:00–03:00 CT. Batch posting may be delayed. This notice is shown once per sign-on.
declared_recoveries.description: A one-time System Notice interstitial appears the first time Member Servicing is opened after sign-on, warning of a scheduled maintenance window. It must be cleared by clicking 'Acknowledge and Continue' before the Member Lookup page is usable. It does not reappear later in the same session.

declared_failures.name: host_transaction_error
declared_failures.message: The application displayed 'Application Error' / 'SYSTEM ERROR MC-5001' with the text: 'The host transaction could not be completed. Contact the service desk with this reference.' This is a genuine host-level fault (not a legitimate business answer) and any run encountering it must stop rather than be treated as a completed lookup.
